messages:
customer-rep (acme): Heads-up — customer upgraded to @redwood/sdk v3.0.0-beta and after deploying to Next.js Edge (Turbopack + pnpm) they see intermittent 401s. Retries kick in and token usage/billing spiked overnight. Repro steps attached below.

maya (support): Ugh. Do we have a minimal repro link or package.json from their build?

customer-rep (acme): Quick repro: Next.js 14 edge function, pnpm + turbopack, import like: `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference'`. Works locally but in prod edge we get: `AuthError: missing token` in stack trace pointing to `node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.mjs`.

eli (eng-runtime): Can you paste the package.json exports/fields and which SDK exact version they installed? Also node / edge runtime target?

customer-rep (acme): They installed `redwood-inference@3.0.0-beta` (release tag). package.json: ```json
{
  "name": "acme-edge",
  "dependencies": {
    "redwood-inference": "3.0.0-beta"
  }
}
```

customer-rep (acme): The library package's package.json exports section (from their node_modules) looks like: ```json
"exports": {
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./auth-shim": {
    "types": "./dist/auth-shim.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/auth-shim.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/auth-shim.cjs"
  },
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  }
}
```

maya (support): Thanks. That exports map looks reasonable at first glance. What does the edge stack show?

customer-rep (acme): Stack: `AuthError: token not found` -> `at Object.getAuth (./dist/index.mjs:45:12)` -> `at RedwoodClient.request (./dist/index.mjs:200:7)` — interestingly the trace points to index.mjs not auth-shim.

eli (eng-runtime): Hypothesis: Turbopack/pnpm is resolving the entrypoint to the ESM `index.mjs` (ok) but is tree-shaking or bundling away the side-effecting auth shim (auth-shim provides runtime detection code that reads env or Edge secrets). If bundler drops it, the runtime callsite never sets the token. This would produce missing token + retries.

nina (devx): We've seen bundlers prefer `types` subfields in some edge toolchains when doing resolution heuristics which can cause odd behaviour for deep imports. Also if auth-shim is only referenced via a dynamic import or a side-effect in CJS, some bundlers drop it unless package.json has `sideEffects` or the import is statically present.

maya (support): Customer: can you check if their built server bundle includes anything from `dist/auth-shim`? `grep -R "auth-shim" .next/edge` in the build output should show it.

customer-rep (acme): Ran grep — nothing. The bundle does contain parts of `dist/index.mjs` but no auth-shim.

eli (eng-runtime): That confirms it. Workarounds: 1) Pin to `redwood-inference@2.9.4` (previous packaging) — that avoids the new exports layout. 2) Force include the shim by adding an explicit import in the app entry: `import 'redwood-inference/auth-shim';` (adds side-effect, preventing removal). 3) Quick server env workaround: set REDWOOD_API_KEY in the runtime env so the client doesn't need shim discovery.

maya (support): For the billing spike we should advise reducing retries client-side until a patch is out. Recommend setting retries to 1 and enabling exponential backoff: ```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ retries: 1, backoffMs: 200 });
```

customer-rep (acme): Pinning to 2.9.4 fixed the immediate 401s. They accepted that as temporary. They asked if we plan a patch.

eli (eng-runtime): Root cause: packaging change in v3.0.0-beta where `auth-shim` became a deep export that is only referenced dynamically. Turbopack's tree-shaker removed it. We'll push a patch to ensure the shim is always preserved and to add `sideEffects` to package.json (or make the shim import static). Also will add CI test with Turbopack + pnpm to catch regressions.

nina (devx): Proposed immediate patch (v3.0.1):
1) Add `"sideEffects": ["./dist/auth-shim.*"]` to package.json.
2) Update index entry to do a static import: `import './auth-shim';` at top-level so bundlers cannot drop it.
3) Add explicit note in changelog about edge bundlers.

eli (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR and ship a canary. Also adding a step to our release checklist: verify deep exports against Turbopack and esbuild.

maya (support): Customer updated to pinned 2.9.4 and reduced retries — billing spike contained. They're ok waiting for v3.0.1. Please link PR once ready so I can follow up. :thumbsup:

build-bot: CI run for PR #489 — canary build artifact: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/489/canary.zip

eli (eng-runtime): PR #489 opened, includes package.json sideEffects + static import. ETA for publish: 48–72h after review.

maya (support): Thanks team — I'll keep the customer posted and log this as "packaging auth-shim dropped by bundler" in the incident notes.

customer-rep (acme): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Workaround notes saved.

nina (devx): Follow-up action: add a small integration e2e that builds a Next.js Edge app with Turbopack + pnpm in our ci-smoke matrix.

maya (support): Closing on our side once v3.0.1 is published and customer confirms.
